as_read: Zeaxanthin alone has one 8-person open-label dose comparison in macular telangiectasia showing no visual benefit; everything else read tests lutein plus zeaxanthin, usually on other nutrients, and its primary clinical results are null.

quote.text: Based on the current study, zeaxanthin supplementation does not result in any visual benefit in patients with macular telangiectasia Type 2 and does not reestablish a normal peaked distribution of MP in the fovea.

proposed_decision_text: These 32 labels print zeaxanthin in three ways: zeaxanthin as the only row at 5 mg (11 labels), zeaxanthin or zeaxanthin isomers beside lutein at 200 mcg to 5 mg (15 labels), and meso-zeaxanthin in multi-ingredient eye formulas (6 labels). No study read meets the bar of a human RCT of zeaxanthin alone with a named primary outcome and a direction. Abstracts only. The only trial of zeaxanthin alone randomized 8 patients with macular telangiectasia type 2 to 10 mg or 20 mg a day, open label with no placebo and no named primary, and found no visual benefit (PMID 28079755). AREDS2 tested lutein 10 mg plus zeaxanthin 2 mg added to an AREDS formula in 4203 people at risk of advanced AMD, and its primary comparison showed no significant reduction (HR 0.90, P = .12) (PMID 23644932). AREDS2 reports also found no significant effect on cataract surgery or vision loss (PMID 23645227), cognition (PMID 26305649) or cardiovascular disease (PMID 24638908). Meta-analyses of lutein and zeaxanthin report better visual acuity and contrast sensitivity in AMD (PMID 25515572) and higher macular pigment (PMID 34157098, PMID 27420092), and a glaucoma trial of lutein, zeaxanthin and meso-zeaxanthin raised macular pigment (PMID 36247822); all test combinations, and macular pigment is a surrogate. A trial of goji berry tested food with lutein (PMID 35044504), a skin trial tested a mixed formula (PMID 27312122), and a crossover measured bioavailability (PMID 29185931). The evidence read does not show a benefit of zeaxanthin alone at the amounts these labels print.

stop_list: Zeaxanthin Isomers beside lutein, 4 labels: 269708 (4 mg), 321608, 46276, 66348 (5 mg). Zeaxanthin beside lutein, 11 labels: 294007, 295527 (2 mg), 312973, 294414, 294415 (200 mcg), 60833 (240 mcg), 311941, 326263, 326264, 269675 (4 mg), 26111 (5 mg). AREDS2 is the nearest match in amount for 294007 and 295527, but it was added to an AREDS formula, so it isn't the ingredient alone.

Meso-zeaxanthin, 6 labels: 62075, 63702 (Meso-Zeaxanthin & Trans-Zeaxanthin Blend 4 mg, 16 to 17 rows), 60779, 60783 (Meso-Zeaxanthin 4 mg plus Trans-Zeaxanthin with no amount, 7 to 8 rows), 307645, 321955 (Zeaxanthin 13 mg plus Meso-Zeaxanthin 9 mg, 6 rows). No trial read tests meso-zeaxanthin alone.
Amounts in mcg stay as printed; none converted.
clinician_items: 28079755: one patient developed a reversible crystalline maculopathy on 20 mg/day zeaxanthin, resolved several months after stopping.
35653117: AREDS2 long-term follow-up; beta carotene nearly doubled lung cancer risk, with no significant increase with lutein/zeaxanthin.
24638908: no differences in adverse events by treatment group.
36247822: no serious adverse events in the glaucoma trial.
